checks.finding: REQ-001..REQ-007 each specify concrete patterns (e.g. id `^CONCEPT-[A-Z][A-Z0-9-]*$`), exact required/optional field sets, minLength/minItems rules, and a fail-closed exit-code contract for the validator (REQ-004). Edge Cases and Field Definitions further pin down borderline behavior (empty concepts[], self-referencing distinguished_from, oversized input). All in-scope requirements give the implementer/verifier a concrete, observable target.

requirements.md REQ-005(b) states: '(b) Book/Bookshelf の正例（Book.must_not_own に display position、Placement concept が並び責務を持つ）' — an explicit requirement that the Book concept's must_not_own be populated with 'display position'. acceptance-tests.md AC-004 (the only AC mapped to REQ-005(b), column value literally 'REQ-005(b)') was rewritten this round to state: '本 fixture は concept の optional フィールドを 1 つも持たない状態とし、must_not_own・stakeholder_perspectives・distinguished_from の 3 キーをいずれも欠落させる' — i.e. Book must have NO must_not_own at all. The string 'display position' does not appear anywhere in acceptance-tests.md (verified by grep), so no other AC covers REQ-005(b)'s content claim either. A task author or verifier reading REQ-005(b) and AC-004 together gets contradictory instructions: populate Book.must_not_own with a specific value, or leave must_not_own entirely absent from every concept in the fixture including Book. This is a genuine contradiction introduced by this round's fix (which correctly resolved the prior AC-003/AC-004-pairing gap but broke traceability of REQ-005(b)'s specific content), confined to the two Phase-1 artifacts this gate owns, so it is properly a spec-review finding rather than a downstream design ambiguity.

Acceptance criteria are phrased in terms of exit codes, stderr line format ('1 行 1 件'), literal field names, and value-retention checks (e.g. AC-003/AC-025 confirm input values are preserved after acceptance). The Positive-capability matrix rows for G1's populated/absent states (rows 3 and 4) now literally name must_not_own / stakeholder_perspectives / distinguished_from in AC-003's and AC-004's own Test Target text in the correct states, closing the round-2 overclaim finding for those rows specifically.

Non-goals explicitly excludes concept-test skill/bootstrap integration, interviewer/template changes, reviewer A/B check additions, reverse mode/C4 separation, v1->v2 migration tooling (INV-009), domain/ markdown artifact generation, and meta.status approval enforcement mechanisms — each tied to a named future Phase or explicit owner decision, preventing scope creep into this Phase-0 feature.

Security Boundaries states content-as-data handling, read-only/no-network/no-external-dependency validator constraints, and a no-secrets fixture rule. Roles and Permissions explicitly states that meta.status Approved has no mechanical enforcement and that approval is human-review-only (citing INV-008), with new enforcement machinery explicitly declared a non-goal. REQ-007 plus AC-002's SHA-256 drift lock make the v1-compatibility constraint concretely testable.

R1, R2, R3 each name a concrete mitigation tied to a validation surface already present in the AC set: R1 to the fixture corpus (REQ-005/AC-003..025), R2 to REQ-006's drift-lock test between validator and schema, R3 to AC-013's sh/ps1 twin-parity check.

investigation.md INV-009 records that sdd-forge has no domain/ directory at the repository root ('sdd-forge 自身に domain/ ディレクトリは存在せず（ルート直下確認）'), so the Approved domain-context-map.md / domain-contract.json precondition for this check is absent. Skip condition applies.
